Larsen, J., Herndon, W., Grant, M. and Marsters, P. (2019). Capturing Leadership: Policies for the US to Advance Direct Air Capture Technology. Rhodium Group, LLC, May 2019. Prepared for Carbon180.

Targeted pass over the 68-page policy report; numbers sit in the Technical Appendix. Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 3). Loaded: first megaton-scale (1 Mt/yr) liquid-solvent and solid-sorbent DAC plants - capital cost low/mid/high and non-energy O&M (Table A.3), capture-cost range over 9 scenarios (Table A.5), financing (11.55%, 30 yr, 90% utilisation) and learning rates; the 9th-plant technology-agnostic RIO input (Table A.2) with the report's only energy figures (0.3 MWh electricity and 5.6 MMBtu heat per t CO2). Not loaded: policy chapters, deployment scenarios, Fig. A.1 learning curves (chart). Traps: the capital costs and O&M are NASEM 2018 numbers re-presented (liquid-solvent mid = average of NASEM high and low); no price year on the appendix tables (2018 taken from the report's levelized $2018 figures and flagged); Table A.2 header says "900 million metric tons CO2 capacity" while the text defines a 1 Mt plant; the energy requirement per technology (NASEM min/max) is not printed, only the agnostic median; costs exclude compression, transport and storage (18 USD/t). Authors confirmed from the title page: Larsen first author, so larsen_2019_001.
